## How paying works (#paying)

*Part 1 lists the provincial drug plans Liivv bills directly (`DIRECT_BILLING` in funding-meta.ts; owner answers A6 and B13, 2026-10-06: each Liivv pharmacy is enrolled with its own province's plan), each by the government's own name (`directPlan`, French only where the government prints one), linked to the page that names it; then why Quebec is not on it, and that no federal program, territorial plan or private insurer is. Part 2 is the programs that pay you back: Liivv gives an invoice for the claim (finance team, B13) and promises no claim will be accepted. Part 3, "Liivv Now, Pay Later" (owner answer A5, 2026-10-06), for insulin pump supplies, Omnipod pods included, after customer service checks eligibility; its terms mirror the owner's program, it never uses another company's program name, and under it is the general contact of Bayshore Express Pharmacy (`contact` in 00-shared.md), which passes the question on (B10). In a province, the checker's pump group also says it once, after its intro (`ui.fundingResults.pumpPayLater`), as Liivv's own option, separate from any program; no program card mentions it. No shop strip follows it: the owner removed the pump-supplies strip from this page on 2026-10-07 (note 7); Your Tools card 13 keeps it.*

## The checker (#find-your-coverage)

*Seven questions; only the province is needed, and results show as soon as it is chosen. The progress line counts all seven, province included. The results are grouped in the owner’s order — `nihb`, `vac`, `pump`, `cgm`, `supplies`, `pharmacare`, `privateFirst`, `dtcRdsp` — after a Liivv card for Quebec or a territory, and end with "Can we bill your program for you?". An unanswered or "not sure" answer never hides a card; a program that does not take the reader’s type, therapy or age is left out; a group with programs on record that none of the answers fits says so, with each program’s own `who` line (and its note, where age ruled it out) and a link to the first one’s page; a group with nothing on record says "we’re still checking" and links Diabetes Canada’s 2024 comparisons. The sensor group says sensor programs are mostly for insulin users, and the pump group that pump programs are for people who use insulin, when the reader uses none. The Ontario Drug Benefit strips card is shown quieter for a reader aged 25 to 64, or 24 and under with a private plan, who would qualify only through another ODB route. Every program card shows the date its page was checked, and "Partly confirmed" where the check was partial. The answers stay in the page; nothing is saved or sent, and the page makes no promise about it yet (E-26). "Request a call" renders only once `cdeRequestReason` is on (landing D3).*

- `ui.fundingResults.vacNotType1Body` — The Veterans Affairs Canada benefit we could confirm is for glucose sensors with type 1. Ask Veterans Affairs Canada what your benefits cover for your type of diabetes.
- `ui.fundingResults.notSignedTitle` — {province} hasn’t signed a national pharmacare agreement

- `ui.fundingResults.privateFirstTitle` — Your private plan pays first
- `ui.fundingResults.privateFirstGenericTitle` — If you have private insurance
- `ui.fundingResults.privateFirstGenericBody` — Ask your insurer and your provincial program which one pays first, before you order.
- `ui.fundingResults.dtcType1Body` — With type 1, the CRA treats you as meeting the life-sustaining therapy test, from 2021 on. You still have to apply, online or by phone with the CRA’s digital form, or by mail with form T2201.
- `ui.fundingResults.dtcInsulinBody` — The life-sustaining therapy test asks whether therapy is needed at least 2 times a week, for an average of at least 14 hours a week, for at least 12 months. Time your pump spends delivering insulin doesn’t count. Apply online or by phone with the CRA’s digital form, or by mail with form T2201.
- `ui.fundingResults.dtcOtherBody` — For diabetes, the usual route is the life-sustaining therapy test: therapy needed at least 2 times a week, for an average of at least 14 hours a week, for at least 12 months. Apply online or by phone with the CRA’s digital form, or by mail with form T2201.

**Private insurance first, by province** (`PRIVATE_FIRST`)

- `funding.privateFirst.AB` — Since October 1, 2026, Alberta’s government-sponsored programs, the Insulin Pump Therapy Program included, pay only after any private or workplace plan, so your private plan pays first. Tell your pharmacist about all the coverage you have.
- `funding.privateFirst.NB` — New Brunswick’s Insulin Pump Program covers only the part other insurance doesn’t, so your private plan pays first.
- `funding.privateFirst.NS` — Nova Scotia’s Insulin Pump Program pays after any other coverage you have, so your private plan pays first.
- `funding.privateFirst.PE` — PEI’s Insulin Pump Program takes off what your private insurance covers before it works out its own share, so your private plan pays first. Ask your insurer for written confirmation of your coverage.

## Programs on record

*Every program the checker can show and the federal section prints, in `PROGRAM_META` order. The name is the legal one and is never translated; an official French name, from the government's own site, shows on /fr where there is one (owner answer B25). "Pays" is how the program pays, from its own page — never how Liivv bills — and is reviewer-only. The first source is the card’s link. Phone numbers are the program's own, as its page prints them, each dialled as a tel: link (owner answer B22). Next recheck 2026-11-01: Monthly automated recheck (scheduled), reviewed by the Liivv content owner (core/scripts/check-funding-sources.mjs, which looks for each row's recheck phrases on its pages; owner answer B20).*

### Non-Insured Health Benefits (NIHB) `fed-nihb`

*Official French name:* Programme des services de santé non assurés (SSNA)  
*Federal · groups: nihb · pays: at-the-pharmacy · applies to: anyone in the jurisdiction · checked 2026-10-06*  
*Sources: Non-Insured Health Benefits program for First Nations and Inuit: Pharmacy benefits (Indigenous Services Canada (Non-Insured Health Benefits)); Non-Insured Health Benefits program updates (Indigenous Services Canada (Non-Insured Health Benefits)); Who is eligible for the Non-Insured Health Benefits (NIHB) program for First Nations and Inuit (Indigenous Services Canada (Non-Insured Health Benefits))*  
*Phone (NIHB Call Centre (Express Scripts Canada), client inquiries / Centre d’appels d’Express Scripts Canada pour le programme des SSNA, ligne de demandes de renseignements pour les clients): 1-888-441-4777 (tollFree) — as printed on Contact the Non-Insured Health Benefits program (Indigenous Services Canada (Non-Insured Health Benefits))*  
*Recheck phrases: "generally send in claims to bill the NIHB program directly"; "when not available through provincial or territorial health insurance"; "FreeStyle Libre 3" on isc-nihb-updates; "800 test strips per 100 days" on isc-nihb-updates; "1-888-441-4777" on isc-nihb-contact*

- `funding.programs.fed-nihb.covered` — NIHB continues to cover these glucose sensors (CGM) for clients who manage their diabetes with insulin: FreeStyle Libre 2, Dexcom G6 and G7, and Guardian Connect. FreeStyle Libre 3 with prior approval, at one reader every 3 years and 14 sensors every 6 months. Guardian 4, as a limited use benefit with prior approval, for people with type 1 aged 19 or under on intensive insulin who use a MiniMed 780G. If you use insulin, test strips up to 800 every 100 days.
- `funding.programs.fed-nihb.who` — Who is eligible is set out on Indigenous Services Canada’s NIHB pages. Liivv can’t decide whether you’re eligible: ask NIHB or your pharmacy.
- `funding.programs.fed-nihb.howToApply` — NIHB covers items on its Drug Benefit List when they aren’t covered by provincial or territorial health insurance, private insurance or another public plan. Pharmacies enrolled with NIHB generally bill it directly, so you don’t pay a deductible or co-payment: you show your client identification. Some items, such as some sensors, need prior approval first.

### Veterans Affairs Canada — continuous glucose monitors (type 1 diabetes), benefit 401140 `fed-vac`

*Official French name:* Anciens Combattants Canada — systèmes de surveillance de la glycémie en continu (diabète de type 1), 401140  
*Federal · groups: vac · pays: unconfirmed · applies to: types: type1 · checked 2026-10-06*  
*Sources: Diabetic supplies: continuous glucose monitors (type 1 diabetes) (Veterans Affairs Canada); Medical Supplies – General (POC 7) (Veterans Affairs Canada)*  
*Phone (Veterans Affairs Canada / Anciens Combattants Canada): 1-866-522-2122 (tollFree) — as printed on Contact us (Veterans Affairs Canada) (Veterans Affairs Canada)*  
*Recheck phrases: "401140"; "1/5 CY"; "PRESCRIBER NOT REQUIRED FOR REPLACEMENT DEVICE"; "diabetic test strips" on vac-poc7-medical-supplies; "1-866-522-2122" on vac-contact*

- `funding.programs.fed-vac.covered` — A continuous glucose monitor for type 1 diabetes, under benefit code 401140, once every 5 calendar years, with a prescription from a doctor or nurse practitioner. A replacement device doesn’t need a new prescription.
- `funding.programs.fed-vac.who` — If you’re a Veterans Affairs Canada client with type 1 diabetes, this benefit may cover you. Ask Veterans Affairs Canada whether it applies to you.
- `funding.programs.fed-vac.howToApply` — It needs pre-authorization, so get that before you buy.
- `funding.programs.fed-vac.notes` — Veterans Affairs Canada’s general medical supplies policy also names diabetic test strips, syringes and needles among its examples.

### Assistive Devices Program — insulin pumps and supplies `on-adp-pump`

*Official French name:* Programme d’appareils et accessoires fonctionnels (PAAF) — pompes à insuline et fournitures  
*Ontario · groups: pump · pays: paid-to-you · applies to: types: type1; therapies: pump; also shown, quieter, to a reader on injections · checked 2026-10-06*  
*Sources: Diabetes equipment and supplies (Government of Ontario)*  
*Phone (Assistive Devices Program / Programme d’appareils et accessoires fonctionnels): 1-800-268-6021 (tollFree), 416-327-8804 (phone, Toronto) — as printed on Preventing and living with diabetes (Government of Ontario)*  
*Recheck phrases: "100% of the ADP price of an insulin pump"; "paid to you in $600 installments every 3 months"; "We do not consider your income"; "We do not cover costs to replace a lost pump"; "1-800-268-6021" on on-preventing-and-living-with-diabetes*

- `funding.programs.on-adp-pump.covered` — 100% of the ADP price of an insulin pump. For pump supplies, up to $2,400 a year, paid to you as $600 every 3 months.
- `funding.programs.on-adp-pump.who` — People with type 1 diabetes who meet the program’s medical criteria. It isn’t based on income. If WSIB or Veterans Affairs Canada already pays for the same items, ADP doesn’t.
- `funding.programs.on-adp-pump.howToApply` — An ADP-registered diabetes education program assesses you, and an ADP-registered vendor sends in the application. ADP aims to review applications within 8 weeks, and the first $600 is sent within 30 days of approval. Renew pump supplies every year.
- `funding.programs.on-adp-pump.notes` — After the 5-year warranty, a worn-out pump can be replaced; ADP asks for a repair quote. A replacement is also covered if your medical needs have changed. ADP doesn’t cover replacing a lost pump or supplies, or repairing ones damaged through misuse or neglect.

### BC PharmaCare — insulin pumps and insulin pump supplies `bc-pharmacare-pumps`

*British Columbia · groups: pump · pays: vendor · applies to: therapies: pump; also shown, quieter, to a reader on injections · checked 2026-10-06*  
*Sources: Insulin pumps and insulin pump supplies (BC PharmaCare) (Government of British Columbia (PharmaCare)); SA for Insulin Pumps (BC PharmaCare) (Government of British Columbia (PharmaCare)); Diabetes product identification numbers (PINs) (Government of British Columbia (PharmaCare))*  
*Phone (BC PharmaCare): 604-683-7151 (phone, Lower Mainland), 1-800-663-7100 (tollFreeIn) — as printed on Contact BC PharmaCare (Government of British Columbia (PharmaCare))*  
*Recheck phrases: "PharmaCare covers 70% of eligible costs"; "Special Authority pre-approval is not required for insulin pump supplies"; "PharmaCare cannot provide retroactive coverage"; "submit claims on PharmaNet"; "one insulin pump every five years" on bc-sa-insulin-pumps; "1-800-663-7100" on bc-pharmacare-contact*

- `funding.programs.bc-pharmacare-pumps.covered` — One insulin pump every 5 years: the Omnipod 5 or Omnipod DASH system, the mylife YpsoPump, or the MiniMed 670G, 770G or 780G. On Fair PharmaCare you pay until you reach your deductible, then PharmaCare pays 70%, and 100% once you reach your family maximum. On Plans B, C, F and W it pays 100%. Pump supplies (pods, infusion sets, reservoirs and cartridges) are covered whether or not PharmaCare paid for your pump, with no Special Authority needed; batteries and adhesive pads aren’t.
- `funding.programs.bc-pharmacare-pumps.who` — People covered by Fair PharmaCare or Plan B, C, F or W, with type 1 or another form of diabetes that needs insulin, whose endocrinologist or diabetes specialist confirms they meet the medical criteria.
- `funding.programs.bc-pharmacare-pumps.howToApply` — Your specialist sends PharmaCare a Special Authority request. If it’s approved, you get a copy of the approval letter to take to the pump maker; the approval lasts 6 months. Wait for the letter before you buy: PharmaCare can’t cover a pump bought before approval. Pump supplies are covered when a pharmacy or an approved pump vendor submits the claim on PharmaNet; PharmaCare doesn’t take paper claims for them.
- `funding.programs.bc-pharmacare-pumps.notes` — No Tandem pump is on PharmaCare’s list of covered pumps. Tandem pump supplies, such as t:slim cartridges and AutoSoft, TruSteel and VariSoft infusion sets, are on its list of diabetes products.

### Insulin Pump Therapy Program (IPTP) `ab-iptp`

*Alberta · groups: pump · pays: vendor · applies to: types: type1, other; therapies: pump; also shown, quieter, to a reader on injections · checked 2026-10-06*  
*Sources: Specialized drug benefits (Alberta) (Government of Alberta); Insulin Pump Therapy Program Eligibility Criteria (Alberta, August 2023) (Government of Alberta); Reference Guide for Alberta Pharmacies (Alberta Blue Cross) (Alberta Blue Cross (for the Government of Alberta))*  
*Phone (Alberta Blue Cross): 1-800-661-6995 (phone) — as printed on Continuous glucose monitor (CGM) coverage for Albertans (December 16, 2025) (Government of Alberta (Ministry of Primary and Preventative Health Services))*  
*Recheck phrases: "type 1 or type 3c diabetes"; "Omnipod 5 Insulin Management System"; "will not be reimbursed for IPT supplies or an insulin pump paid by them personally" on ab-iptp-eligibility-2023; "operate as the payor of last resort" on abc-pharmacy-reference-guide; "1-800-661-6995" on ab-cgm-fact-sheet-2025*

- `funding.programs.ab-iptp.covered` — An insulin pump every 5 years from an approved maker (Medtronic, Ypsomed, Insulet or Tandem), its supplies, and other diabetes management supplies, up to set limits.
- `funding.programs.ab-iptp.who` — Alberta residents enrolled in, or eligible for, the Alberta Health Care Insurance Plan, with type 1 or type 3c diabetes, who meet the program’s clinical criteria. Adults have a review every year, and children under 18 every 6 months.
- `funding.programs.ab-iptp.howToApply` — Through an approved insulin pump clinic: you attend a pre-pump information session, complete an education plan, have at least one assessment and sign a Patient Responsibility Form. The clinic then sends Alberta Blue Cross an eligibility form, and Alberta Blue Cross mails you a confirmation letter. Pumps come straight from an approved maker, and supplies from a licensed Alberta pharmacy or an approved maker, which bill the program directly. The program doesn’t pay you back for a pump or supplies you pay for yourself.
- `funding.programs.ab-iptp.notes` — Since October 1, 2026, Alberta’s government programs, this one included, pay only after any private or workplace plan you have.

- `funding.programs.mb-pump.covered` — One approved insulin pump every 5 years, ordered from an approved supplier at no cost to you, with no deductible. Pump supplies aren’t part of it: they can be covered by Manitoba Pharmacare, where your deductible applies.

### Insulin Pump Access Program `qc-pump`

*Official French name:* Programme d’accès aux pompes à insuline

- `funding.programs.qc-pump.covered` — Up to $6,300 toward a pump every 5 years, and up to $4,000 a year for pump supplies.
- `funding.programs.qc-pump.who` — You have to join before you turn 18. You can stay in after 18, with a review each year. Adults diagnosed later can’t join.
- `funding.programs.qc-pump.howToApply` — For supplies, send your original receipts or insurance statements to the program’s paying agent, the CHU de Québec – Université Laval. With some companies you don’t pay for supplies at all, because the CHU refunds the company directly.
- `funding.programs.qc-pump.notes` — The program’s page was last updated on February 19, 2021, so check the current amounts with the program.

### New Brunswick Insulin Pump Program (IPP) `nb-ipp`

*Official French name:* Le Programme de pompes à insuline (PPI) du Nouveau-Brunswick

- `funding.programs.nb-ipp.covered` — Insulin pumps, pump supplies and glucose sensors (CGM), for the part that isn’t covered by other insurance.
- `funding.programs.nb-ipp.who` — Pumps: type 1, at any age. Sensors: type 1, or type 2 with 3 or more insulin injections a day. It’s based on income, and private insurance has to be used first. If your insurance already covers 100% of the cost, you can’t join.
- `funding.programs.nb-ipp.howToApply` — For pumps, an endocrinologist, internist or pediatrician confirms you meet the medical criteria; for sensors, the health care provider who manages your diabetes does. If you apply for both, the same specialist confirms both. Then you apply online. Devices and supplies come only from the program’s approved vendors, not from pharmacies. You pay your share to the vendor, and the vendor bills the province for the rest.

### Nova Scotia Insulin Pump Program `ns-ipp`

*Nova Scotia · groups: pump · pays: unconfirmed · applies to: types: type1; therapies: pump; also shown, quieter, to a reader on injections · checked 2026-10-06*

*Recheck phrases: "1 insulin pump every 5 years"; "There are no premiums or deductibles"; "Clinical Eligibility Form"; "It should take 1 to 2 weeks"; "1-855-306-6360" on ns-health-contacts*

- `funding.programs.ns-ipp.covered` — One insulin pump every 5 years (Tandem, Medtronic or Insulet), plus pump supplies. You pay a yearly share based on your income and family size, with no premiums or deductibles.
- `funding.programs.ns-ipp.who` — People with type 1 diabetes, diagnosed at least 4 months ago.
- `funding.programs.ns-ipp.howToApply` — Contact the Insulin Pump Program to confirm you’re eligible. It connects you with an approved Diabetes Health Centre, which completes and sends a Clinical Eligibility Form for you. Then fill in the funding application (one form for adults, one for children and youth) and mail it with your supporting documents. A decision takes about 1 to 2 weeks. Renew between January 1 and March 31 every year.
- `funding.programs.ns-ipp.notes` — Glucose sensors aren’t part of this program. Nova Scotia has a separate Sensor-based Glucose Monitoring Program, shown under sensor programs.

### PEI Insulin Pump Program `pe-ipp`

*Prince Edward Island · groups: pump · pays: vendor · applies to: types: type1; therapies: pump; also shown, quieter, to a reader on injections · checked 2026-10-06*

- `funding.programs.pe-ipp.covered` — Up to 100% of the cost of a pump and its supplies, shipped every 3 months, depending on your household income, any private insurance and the device’s cost. Approved pumps: Medtronic, Omnipod and Tandem. Glucose sensors aren’t part of it: PEI has a separate Glucose Sensor Program.
- `funding.programs.pe-ipp.who` — PEI residents of any age with type 1 diabetes whom the Provincial Diabetes Program finds medically eligible.
- `funding.programs.pe-ipp.howToApply` — Your family doctor or nurse practitioner can refer you to the Provincial Diabetes Program, whose team decides whether you’re medically eligible. You then complete the program’s application with your pump team. You pay your share straight to the pump company, usually every 3 months before your supplies ship. Renew every year between April 1 and June 30.
- `funding.programs.pe-ipp.notes` — If you have private insurance, its share is taken off before the program works out its own, so ask your insurer for written confirmation of your coverage. What you pay for the pump or its supplies doesn’t count toward the Catastrophic Drug Program’s household cap.

- `funding.programs.qc-cgm.covered` — FreeStyle Libre 3 Plus (listed since December 11, 2025) and Dexcom G6 and G7 are on Quebec’s public plan list as exception drugs. Since February 4, 2026, the same criteria apply to every continuous glucose monitor on the list.
- `funding.programs.qc-cgm.who` — People 2 and over. Under 18: type 1 diabetes. 18 and over: intensive insulin therapy (an insulin pump, or at least 3 injections a day of at least 2 different insulins), plus at least one of these: an A1C that stays above your target despite optimal care, frequent lows in the past year, or not being able to recognize or report the signs of a low.
- `funding.programs.qc-cgm.howToApply` — Your prescriber asks for coverage as an exception. The first approval lasts 6 months. It’s renewed if you wear the sensor at least 70% of the time.
- `funding.programs.qc-cgm.notes` — Quebec’s public plan generally doesn’t cover prescription drugs bought outside Quebec. Check the details with RAMQ.

### Sensor-based Glucose Monitoring Program `ns-sbgm`

*Nova Scotia · groups: cgm · pays: at-the-pharmacy · applies to: types: type1, type2; therapies: insulinInjections, pump · checked 2026-10-06*  
*Sources: Apply for the Sensor-based Glucose Monitoring Program (Nova Scotia) (Government of Nova Scotia); Department of Health and Wellness: contacts (Nova Scotia) (Government of Nova Scotia)*  
*Phone (Sensor-based Glucose Monitoring Program): 902-496-5667 (phone), 1-877-330-0323 (tollFree) — as printed on Department of Health and Wellness: contacts (Nova Scotia) (Government of Nova Scotia)*  
*Recheck phrases: "There are no premiums or copayments"; "at least 4 injections per day"; "$150,000 or less"; "only covered when dispensed by a pharmacy with a prescription"; "1-877-330-0323" on ns-health-contacts*

- `funding.programs.ns-sbgm.covered` — Approved sensors and supplies listed in the Nova Scotia Formulary, dispensed by a pharmacy with a prescription. There’s a yearly deductible based on family income: $0 up to $60,000, $500 up to $80,000, $750 up to $100,000 and $1,000 up to $150,000. There are no premiums or co-payments.
- `funding.programs.ns-sbgm.who` — Nova Scotia residents aged 2 and over with a valid Health Card and a household income of $150,000 or less, with type 1 or type 2 diabetes on intensive insulin therapy (at least 4 injections a day) or an insulin pump.
- `funding.programs.ns-sbgm.howToApply` — Fill in the registration form (a doctor, nurse practitioner or pharmacist completes its last page) and submit it online or by mail. Enrolment takes 1 to 2 weeks and renews automatically each February. You pay the full cost at the pharmacy until you reach your deductible.
- `funding.programs.ns-sbgm.notes` — Private insurance has to be used first. The program doesn’t cover prescriptions bought outside Nova Scotia except in very specific cases.

### Provincial Continuous Glucose Monitoring Program `nl-cgm`

*Newfoundland and Labrador · groups: cgm · pays: unconfirmed · applies to: types: type1 · checked 2026-10-06 · **partly confirmed** (the card says to check with the program)*  
*Sources: Provincial Continuous Glucose Monitoring Program (Newfoundland and Labrador, 2025) (Government of Newfoundland and Labrador)*  
*Recheck phrases: "same income-testing as the NL Insulin Pump Program"*

- `funding.programs.nl-cgm.covered` — Full or partial coverage of glucose sensors (CGM).
- `funding.programs.nl-cgm.who` — In May 2025, the province announced that from fall 2025 the program would be open to everyone with type 1 diabetes who meets its medical and income criteria.
- `funding.programs.nl-cgm.notes` — The program started in 2023 for children with type 1. In 2024 it grew to include young people up to age 24, and pregnancy and gestational diabetes. Ask the program what it covers for you now.

### Ontario Drug Benefit — blood glucose test strips `on-odb-strips`

*Official French name:* Programme de médicaments de l’Ontario (PMO) — bandelettes de test de glycémie  
*Ontario · groups: supplies · pays: at-the-pharmacy · applies to: types: type1, type2, other · checked 2026-10-06*

*Phone (Ontario Drug Benefit Program / Programme de médicaments de l’Ontario): 1-888-405-0405 (tollFree), 416-503-4586 (phone, Toronto) — as printed on Get coverage for prescription drugs (Government of Ontario)*  
*Recheck phrases: "with insulin 3,000"; "other diabetic supplies are not covered by the ODB program"; "1-888-405-0405"*

- `funding.programs.on-odb-strips.covered` — Test strips each year: 3,000 if you use insulin; 400 if you take a diabetes medicine with a higher risk of lows; 200 with a lower-risk medicine; 200 if you manage with diet and lifestyle alone. More needs a reason from your doctor or nurse practitioner.
- `funding.programs.on-odb-strips.who` — People covered by the Ontario Drug Benefit. That includes people 65 and over, and people 24 and under with no private plan (OHIP+).

### Monitoring for Health Program `on-mfhp`

*Official French name:* Programme de surveillance pour une bonne santé de l’Ontario  
*Ontario · groups: supplies · pays: receipts · applies to: therapies: insulinInjections, pump · checked 2026-10-06*  
*Sources: Preventing and living with diabetes (Government of Ontario); Ontario Monitoring for Health Program (Diabetes Canada, running an Ontario government program)*  
*Phone (Diabetes Canada / Diabète Canada): 1-800-361-0796 (phone) — as printed on Preventing and living with diabetes (Government of Ontario)*  
*Recheck phrases: "can only submit to this program for lancets and/or a blood glucose meter"; "must be signed by a doctor or nurse practitioner"; "$920"; "1-800-361-0796"*

- `funding.programs.on-mfhp.covered` — 75% of the cost of a blood glucose meter, up to $75 once every 5 years, and 75% of the cost of test strips and lancets, up to $920 a year. For a talking meter, if a letter from your doctor confirms visual impairment, up to $300 once every 5 years.
- `funding.programs.on-mfhp.who` — People who use insulin (type 1 or type 2), and people with gestational diabetes, who have no other coverage for these supplies. If you’re 65 or over, on social assistance or a Trillium Drug Program client, you can claim only for lancets and a blood glucose meter.
- `funding.programs.on-mfhp.howToApply` — Diabetes Canada runs this program for Ontario. Your first claim form has to be signed by a doctor or nurse practitioner. Mail in the claim form with your original receipts. Processing takes about 8 weeks.

*Official French name:* Programme d’appareils et accessoires fonctionnels (PAAF) — seringues et aiguilles pour les aînés

*Recheck phrases: "you can apply for $170 annually to help pay for syringes and needles"; "You must renew with the ADP every 2 years for syringes and needles"*

- `funding.programs.on-adp-seniors.covered` — $170 a year toward insulin syringes and needles.
- `funding.programs.on-adp-seniors.who` — People 65 and over who need insulin every day and live at home.
- `funding.programs.on-adp-seniors.howToApply` — Buy them from any retailer in Ontario that sells them. Renew every 2 years. ADP pays you by direct deposit or cheque.

### BC PharmaCare — diabetes supplies `bc-np-supplies`

*British Columbia · groups: supplies · pays: at-the-pharmacy · applies to: anyone in the jurisdiction · checked 2026-10-06*

- `funding.programs.bc-np-supplies.who` — You need training from a diabetes education centre or primary care network first. If you’re not on Plan C, F or W, register for Fair PharmaCare.

### Newfoundland and Labrador Prescription Drug Program (NLPDP) — blood glucose test strips `nl-strips`

*Official French name:* Programme de médicaments sur ordonnance de Terre-Neuve-et-Labrador (NLPDP) — bandelettes de test de glycémie  
*Newfoundland and Labrador · groups: supplies · pays: at-the-pharmacy · applies to: anyone in the jurisdiction · checked 2026-10-06*

*Recheck phrases: "Diabetic Test Strips"; "A paid claim for insulin and/or non-insulin diabetic medication within the past year"; "Payor of Last Resort"; "The NLPDP is payor of last resort" on nl-prescription-drug-program*

- `funding.programs.nl-strips.covered` — Test strips a year: 2,500 with short-acting insulin; 700 with long-acting insulin only, plus 100 more with Special Authorization; 100 with non-insulin diabetes medicines only, plus 50; 50 with no diabetes medicine, plus 50 (fills 6 months apart). In pregnancy with gestational or type 2 diabetes, the quantity your health professional asks for.
- `funding.programs.nl-strips.who` — People covered by the Newfoundland and Labrador Prescription Drug Program. A strip claim is paid only if a claim for a diabetes medicine was paid for you in the past year, or you have Special Authorization.
- `funding.programs.nl-strips.notes` — The program pays last: if you have private insurance, the claim goes there first.

*Official French name:* Programme d’aide pour les personnes atteintes d’une maladie chronique ou d’une incapacité

### Disability tax credit `fed-dtc`

*Official French name:* Crédit d’impôt pour personnes handicapées (CIPH)  
*Federal · groups: dtcRdsp · pays: tax · applies to: anyone in the jurisdiction · checked 2026-10-06*  
*Sources: Life-sustaining therapy (Canada Revenue Agency); How to apply - Disability tax credit form (DTC) (Canada Revenue Agency); Disability-Related Information 2025 (RC4064) (Canada Revenue Agency)*  
*Phone (Canada Revenue Agency / Agence du revenu du Canada): 1-800-959-8281 (phone) — as printed on How to apply - Disability tax credit form (DTC) (Canada Revenue Agency)*  
*Recheck phrases: "People with Type 1 diabetes meet the eligibility criteria under life-sustaining therapy"; "Both Part A and Part B must be submitted using the same method" on cra-dtc-how-to-apply; "1-800-959-8281" on cra-dtc-how-to-apply*

- `funding.programs.fed-dtc.covered` — A tax credit for people whose impairment meets the CRA’s test. For diabetes, the usual route is life-sustaining therapy.
- `funding.programs.fed-dtc.who` — If you have type 1, the CRA treats you as meeting the life-sustaining therapy test, from 2021 on. Otherwise, the therapy has to be needed at least 2 times a week, for an average of at least 14 hours a week, and the need has to have lasted, or be expected to last, at least 12 months. Time your pump spends delivering insulin doesn’t count toward the 14 hours.
- `funding.programs.fed-dtc.howToApply` — Apply online or by phone with the CRA’s digital form, or by mail with the paper form T2201. Both parts of the application have to go in the same way. Even with type 1, you still have to apply.

*Federal · groups: dtcRdsp · pays: tax · applies to: anyone in the jurisdiction · checked 2026-10-06*  
*Sources: Registered Disability Savings Plan: how to apply (Employment and Social Development Canada)*  
*Recheck phrases: "the year they turn 59"; "the year you turn 49"*

- `funding.programs.fed-rdsp.covered` — A long-term savings plan, with government grants and bonds.
- `funding.programs.fed-rdsp.who` — You have to be approved for the Disability Tax Credit first, live in Canada and have a Social Insurance Number. You can open a plan until December 31 of the year you turn 59. Grants and bonds are paid only until the year you turn 49.

## What changed lately

- `ui.fundingPage.changesEyebrow` — What changed lately
- `ui.fundingPage.changesHeading` — Recent changes, with dates
- `ui.fundingPage.changes.1` — April 1, 2024: Northwest Territories Extended Health Benefits became based on income rather than on a list of diseases.  
  *Sources: GNWT finalizes new Extended Health Benefits policy (Government of the Northwest Territories).*
- `ui.fundingPage.changes.2` — October 10, 2024: the federal Pharmacare Act became law.  
  *Sources: Bill C-64, Pharmacare Act (LEGISinfo) (Parliament of Canada (LEGISinfo)).*
- `ui.fundingPage.changes.3` — February 27 to March 20, 2025: Manitoba, British Columbia, Prince Edward Island and Yukon signed national pharmacare agreements.  
  *Sources: National pharmacare bilateral agreements (Health Canada).*
- `ui.fundingPage.changes.4` — April 15, 2025: Manitoba made most diabetes medicines free, with no deductible.  
  *Sources: Manitoba Enhanced Pharmacare Program (MEPP) (Government of Manitoba).*
- `ui.fundingPage.changes.6` — May 2025: Newfoundland and Labrador announced that its sensor program would open to everyone with type 1 who meets its criteria, from fall 2025.  
  *Sources: Provincial Continuous Glucose Monitoring Program (Newfoundland and Labrador, 2025) (Government of Newfoundland and Labrador).*
- `ui.fundingPage.changes.8` — July 31 and November 28, 2025: the Ontario Drug Benefit began covering Dexcom G7, then FreeStyle Libre 3 Plus, for people who take insulin.  
  *Sources: Executive Officer Notice: Funding Continuous Glucose Monitoring Systems through the Ontario Drug Benefit Program (July 24, 2025) (Ontario Ministry of Health); Ontario Drug Benefit Formulary/Comparative Drug Index Edition 43: Summary of Changes, November 2025 (Ontario Ministry of Health).*
- `ui.fundingPage.changes.5` — September 2025: Non-Insured Health Benefits added FreeStyle Libre 3, with prior approval.  
  *Sources: Non-Insured Health Benefits program updates (Indigenous Services Canada (Non-Insured Health Benefits)).*
- `ui.fundingPage.changes.9` — February 4, 2026: Quebec set the same criteria for every continuous glucose monitor on its public plan’s list of exception drugs.  
  *Sources: FreeStyle Libre 3 Plus (surveillance de la glycémie): extract notice to the Minister (Institut national d’excellence en santé et en services sociaux (INESSS), Québec); Dexcom G6 et Dexcom G7 (surveillance glycémie): extract notice to the Minister (Institut national d’excellence en santé et en services sociaux (INESSS), Québec); Extrait d’avis au ministre sur Freestyle Libre 3 Plus (INESSS, décembre 2025) (Institut national d’excellence en santé et en services sociaux (INESSS), Québec).*
- `ui.fundingPage.changes.7` — March 1, 2026: British Columbia made insulin and a set list of diabetes medicines free. Wider device and supply coverage followed on April 1.  
  *Sources: National pharmacare (BC PharmaCare) (Government of British Columbia (PharmaCare)); Enhanced coverage in B.C. supports more people with diabetes (BC Gov News, March 30, 2026) (Government of British Columbia (BC Gov News)).*
- `ui.fundingPage.changes.10` — October 1, 2026: Alberta’s government-sponsored drug programs began paying only after private or workplace insurance.  
  *Sources: Reference Guide for Alberta Pharmacies (Alberta Blue Cross) (Alberta Blue Cross (for the Government of Alberta)); Non-Group Coverage (Alberta) (Government of Alberta).*

## Quebec and the territories

- `ui.fundingPage.whereEyebrow` — Quebec and the territories
- `ui.fundingPage.whereHeading` — Ordering from Quebec or the territories
- `ui.fundingPage.whereBody` — Liivv’s pharmacies serve all of Canada, Quebec and the territories included. Insulin can’t be ordered online for delivery in Quebec. Quebec’s public drug plan generally doesn’t cover prescription drugs bought outside Quebec, so orders shipped to Quebec are paid for privately. In Yukon, the Northwest Territories or Nunavut, you pay for your order yourself: check with your program that it will pay you back, and ask us for an invoice for your claim. Yukon’s Chronic Disease and Disability Benefits Program, for example, needs its approval before you buy outside Yukon, or a claim within 1 year.  
  *Sources: Stays Outside Québec (Gouvernement du Québec); Get help with costs if you have a chronic disease or disability (Yukon) (Government of Yukon). About Liivv, rests on the owner’s word (2026-10-05).*

## When it isn’t enough

*Three cards. The second links its two sources under it.*

- `ui.fundingPage.enoughEyebrow` — When it isn’t enough
- `ui.fundingPage.enoughHeading` — The coverage doesn’t cover it all
- `ui.fundingPage.enough1Heading` — Ask your diabetes education program
- `ui.fundingPage.enough1Body` — They know what gets approved locally, and they’re often the ones who fill in the forms. Diabetes education programs aren’t run by Liivv.  
  *About Liivv, rests on the owner’s word (2026-10-05).*
- `ui.fundingPage.enough2Heading` — Compare provinces with Diabetes Canada
- `ui.fundingPage.enough2Body` — Diabetes Canada publishes side-by-side comparisons of what each province and territory covers, and a report on diabetes out-of-pocket costs. The pump and glucose monitoring comparisons are from 2024, so some recent changes on this page aren’t in them.  
  *Sources: Comparisons by Province/Territory (Diabetes Canada); Diabetes and Diabetes-Related Out-of-Pocket Costs (2022) (Diabetes Canada).*
- `ui.fundingPage.enough3Heading` — Ask a CDE
- `ui.fundingPage.enough3Body` — For questions about pumps, sensors, supplies, billing and claims, Liivv’s Certified Diabetes Educators can help, wherever you are in Canada.

## If you change provinces

- `ui.fundingPage.movingEyebrow` — Moving
- `ui.fundingPage.movingHeading` — If you change provinces
- `ui.fundingPage.movingIntro` — Pump and sensor programs differ from province to province, and several need an assessment by a local diabetes program before they’ll cover anything.  
  *Sources: Diabetes equipment and supplies (Government of Ontario); Insulin Pump Program (Saskatchewan) (Government of Saskatchewan); Health Coverage: Manitoba Adult Insulin Pump Coverage Program (Government of Manitoba); The New Brunswick Insulin Pump Program (IPP) (Government of New Brunswick).*
- `ui.fundingPage.beforeHeading` — Before you go
- `ui.fundingPage.before1` — Send in any claims you still have with your current program.
- `ui.fundingPage.before2` — Ask your diabetes team for a written summary of your devices, supplies and settings.
- `ui.fundingPage.arriveHeading` — When you arrive
- `ui.fundingPage.arrive1` — Check your new province in the checker above.
- `ui.fundingPage.arrive2` — Find a diabetes education program early. Several programs need one to assess you before they’ll pay.

*National, with no "Available in Ontario" label. Under the body, the contact of Liivv’s Certified Diabetes Educators (`contact` in 00-shared.md: phone and hours; owner answers A2, B5, B9, B10, 2026-10-06; owner note 5, 2026-10-07). The "Request a call" button is off until `cdeRequestReason` is switched on (landing D3; B6).*

- `ui.fundingPage.cdeEyebrow` — Anywhere in Canada
- `ui.fundingPage.cdeHeading` — Questions about pumps, sensors, billing or claims
- `ui.fundingPage.cdeBody` — Liivv’s Certified Diabetes Educators answer questions from anywhere in Canada: pumps, sensors, meters, supplies, billing and claims. When needed, they pass you to Liivv’s pharmacy in your province.  
  *About Liivv, rests on the owner’s word (2026-10-05).*
- `ui.fundingPage.cdeCta` — Request a call

- `ui.fundingPage.closingBody` — If the numbers aren’t working, tell your diabetes team. Your diabetes education program may know of routes this page doesn’t cover.

## About this page — the governance block

*It also carries the shared machine-translation notice on /fr and the commercial disclosure (`ui.governance`, in 00-shared.md), and lists every source the page names, once each. No byline or review line renders until a clinician is named.*

- `funding.governance.disclaimer` — This is general information, not medical or financial advice. It isn’t a substitute for care from your diabetes team, doctor or pharmacist, and it doesn’t tell you which device or medicine to use. Programs change their amounts and rules often, so check the official page or ask the program before you plan around a number.

- The focus and vibe notes: the vibe note renders without a label. "The Liivv Vibe" is Ostomy’s word, and Diabetes Care has no label for it.
- The checker rules a program out for a type it does not take before it looks at therapy. The record’s sketch (A.5) checked therapy first, which showed type 1 pump programs to a type 2 reader on injections as "If you’re thinking about a pump".
- "Request a call" (the CDE band and the "Can we bill your program for you?" card) renders only once the appointment page can take the request (`cdeRequestReason` in landing-meta.ts, landing D3; B6), as on the landing. Since 2026-10-06 the CDE band shows the CDE contact in its place: since owner note 5 (2026-10-07), the phone and hours of Liivv’s Certified Diabetes Educators.
- `funding.liivv.pharmacies` renders nowhere today: "Ordering from Quebec or the territories" (`whereBody`) opens with the same sentence (owner answers A1 and B11, 2026-10-06). It is kept for the checker’s Liivv cards if the owner wants it there.
- `funding.liivv.quebecBody` says the Insulin Pump Access Program takes receipts "as shown below". Its card is below only when the reader’s answers leave it in (type 1 or not sure, and a pump or insulin injections).
- On /fr while the `fundingChecker` gate is closed, the section shows each province and territory with its programs by their legal names, each linked to its official page with the date it was checked and its phone numbers, and the "still checking" line for a province with none. No question is asked there, so `toolIntro` and the pump group's intro are left off.
- Owner answer A6 ("We support all provincial pump programs"): in a province, the pump group in the checker opens with `ui.fundingResults.pumpIntro` (each program decides where its supplies come from and how it pays; check its rules before ordering), then `pumpPayLater`, which says once that Liivv Now, Pay Later is Liivv's own way to pay, separate from any program (A5). No program card mentions pay-later (full-site review, 2026-10-06: New Brunswick's program supplies only through its vendors, PEI's co-pay goes to the pump company, and Alberta's pays nothing back for supplies bought privately). In the territories the pump group has no intro: their routes are not provincial programs.
- Phone numbers (B22) render under a program's words on its card, in its federal row and in the /fr plain list, as tel: links (+1 and the ten digits; an extension is printed, and the first one is dialled after a pause, as a comma in the tel: link, since 2026-10-06). An office name is the program's own proper noun, in French only where the government prints one. The engine card part gained an optional `phones` list and a group `intro` line (_microsite/funding/checker-parts.tsx, a Diabetes-first addition to the Ostomy twin).
- The Yukon pump card (`yt-pump`) is partly confirmed: the National Pharmacare page states pump access and the 5-year cycle, but not who pays, how much, or how to apply (verify item 6). yukon.ca refuses plain requests, so the scheduled recheck reports its pages as blocked; they were read in a browser on 2026-10-06.
- The PEI pump card cites the program's questions and answers (PDF, 2026-05-06): the program's web page answers with a CAPTCHA, which nothing here tries to get past.
- No products on this page. The pump-supplies strip that sat between "How paying works" and the checker (#pump-supplies, B21) was removed by the owner on 2026-10-07 (note 7), which closes D-13; the page makes no catalogue request. The same strip, "Pump supplies, by pump.", stays on Your Tools card 13.
- Quebec sensors (`qc-cgm`) rest on INESSS's records of the minister's decisions (RAMQ's own pages refuse requests), so the card stays partly confirmed. Corrected per the verifier: the February 4, 2026 change defines intensive insulin therapy for every CGM; it did not open coverage to type 2 in general.
